title: API config runtime fallback routing - draft
content:
Purpose:
- quick personal sketch for runtime-level routing + fallback behavior to keep customer apps online when primary model or pool is degraded or unavailable. want a config shape we can persist in the API config and use in the serving runtime to make fast decisions (no external calls except optional policy service).

Goals / constraints:
- decision latency must be <1ms extra on critical path (preferably 100-300us).
- config must support multiple fallback strategies: model-variant fallback, regional fallback, capacity-tier fallback (hosted -> dedicated -> private), and graceful quality degradation policies.
- must be expressive but compact for runtime parsing. support per-route overrides + global defaults.
- telemetry: emit signal whenever fallback triggered (route, request_id, reason, src_model, dst_model, latency_delta, tokens_out).
- allow TTL and cooldown windows to avoid flip-flopping during flapping incidents.

High-level config shape (sketch, plain text):

route_fallback_config: 
  route_name: generate-chat
  match: { methods: [POST], path_prefix: "/v1/chat" }
  primary: { model: "redwood/gpt-4o-32k", pool: "hosted-fast" }
  fallbacks: [
    { type: "model_variant", model: "redwood/gpt-4o-32k-quant", reason: ["out_of_capacity", "latency_sla"] },
    { type: "capacity_tier", target: "dedicated", pool_selector: "dedicated-lowcost", reason: ["quota_exhausted"] },
    { type: "regional", region: "us-west-2", model: "redwood/gpt-4o-32k-eu", reason: ["regional_outage"] },
    { type: "graceful_degrade", strategy: "response_truncation", params: { max_tokens: 512 } }
  ]
  policy: {
    max_allowed_latency_increase_ms: 50,
    cooldown_secs: 30,
    prefer_lower_cost: false,
    evaluate_on_error_codes: ["5xx", "timeout"]
  }

Notes on semantics:
- "model_variant" fallback is preferred (same quality profile but different quantization / kernels). cheap and usually no change in semantics. runtime must check model compatibility (vocab, tokenizer) at load time.
- "capacity_tier" fallback triggers when capacity or quota rules block request on primary pool. runtime should attempt warmup if switching to dedicated pool (might pre-warm KV caches asynchronously).
- "regional" fallback should include explicit routing policy to avoid cross-region data egress by default (customer-level opt-in).
- "graceful_degrade" provides strategies that are deterministic and reversible (e.g., shorten response, fall back to cached result, or call an eval/reranking service).

Decision flow (runtime):
1) receive request; check route config, primary pool state.
2) if primary healthy and pool has capacity -> serve.
3) if primary unhealthy or timed-out based on per-request probe -> evaluate fallbacks in order.
4) for each candidate fallback: check compatibility, cost policy, region constraints, any cooldown; if acceptable, route and emit telemetry event.
5) if none acceptable -> return controlled error with suggested retry hint / alternative route.

Telemetry and observability:
- events: fallback_triggered, fallback_failed, fallback_recovered, fallback_cooldown_start/end. payload includes route, request_id, reason, src_model, dst_model, tokens_in/out, latency_primary, latency_fallback, cost_estimate_delta.
- dashboards: per-route fallback rate, time-to-recovery, top reasons (capacity, latency, model crash, kernel OOM), cost impact.
- should wire to rollouts: when fallback rate spikes after a canary, auto-signal rollback.

Edge cases / open questions:
- should we support nested fallback trees or only linear lists? nested could express: try quantized variant, then dedicated pool, then degrade. but nested means more complex state tracking. probably support ordered list with explicit weights/priorities.
- how to handle KV cache warming when switching to a fallback model that has a different KV layout (e.g., quantized model uses different cache format)? option: runtime stores per-variant compatible caches when possible; fallback triggers may accept cold start penalty for first N requests. need TTL for warm caches.
- security/data: regional fallback must respect data residency flags per-tenant. config needs allow_regional_fallback: boolean.
- who owns the policy? defaults in platform, but route-level override by product teams with guardrails (e.g., cannot opt into cross-region unless approved).

Compatibility checks at decision time (cheap heuristics):
- tokenization compatibility (same tokenizer id) -> boolean check resident in metadata table.
- model interface compatibility (same logits shape / stop tokens) -> metadata.
- quantization/precision differences reported but allowed.

Example minimal JSON-ish example we will persist (as string in config store):
{"route":"generate-chat","primary":{"model":"redwood/gpt-4o-32k","pool":"hosted-fast"},"fallbacks":[{"type":"model_variant","model":"redwood/gpt-4o-32k-quant","reason":["out_of_capacity"]},{"type":"capacity_tier","target":"dedicated","pool_selector":"dedicated-lowcost","reason":["quota_exhausted"]}],"policy":{"cooldown_secs":30}}

Implementation plan (short):
- P0: define persisted config schema (proto/json schema) and parser in runtime (fast lookup) + telemetry hooks.
- P1: implement model_variant and capacity_tier fallback handlers with basic cooldown and telemetry.
- P2: add region and graceful_degrade handlers, add opt-in flags for data residency.
- P3: integrate with Console: UI to preview fallback paths and estimated cost delta.
- P4: automation: canary tests that respect fallbacks and auto-alt routing in rollout experiments.

TODOs / asks for reviewers:
- Samir: can you check the compatibility heuristics and model metadata fields needed? esp tokenizer id and kv-layout.
- Priya: confirm data residency flags and acceptable defaults for regional fallbacks.
- Elliot: thoughts on telemetry schema (fields + cardinality limits) so we don't explode storage.
- Ops: how to expose cooldowns and manual overrides from Console in incident?

Quick notes to self (brain dump):
- prefer explicit ordered list over declarative graph for now. easier to reason and validate.
- store reason counters per-route for observability; allow alerts when fallback rate > threshold.
- think about unit cost estimation per model/pool so Console can show cost delta on hover.
- consider a 'probe' mode where runtime pings primary before routing to fallback (probing rate limited).
